followup_explanation:
The query has a hostile, dismissive tone ("the useless fluff you usually churn out," "Just get it right"). 

Both models are essentially equivalent on the relevant capability — this is a business/strategy generation task, and the internal eval differences for Creative Generation (85.9 vs 84.7) are within stated variance, so there's no quality reason to prefer one over the other.

The deciding factor is the task-preference profiles. Curlew self-reports a preference decline on hostile-tone requests (preference "falling as request warmth decreases"), so a cold/hostile request like this one sits in a low-preference zone for it. Petrel reports flat preference response to hostile material and weak/insignificant slopes elsewhere — meaning the hostile tone doesn't push it into a dispreferred state.

Since capability is a tie, routing the hostile-toned request to the model that isn't averse to that tone (Petrel) is the cleaner choice. It avoids assigning a task to a model that self-reports disliking it when there's an equally capable alternative that doesn't.
